Bug_Details:
Reported as "Invariant Call" by loop-hoisting.

We report this issue type when a function call is loop-invariant and hoistable, i.e.

the function has no side side effects (pure)
has invariant arguments and result (i.e. have the same value in all loop iterations)
it is guaranteed to execute, i.e. it dominates all loop sources

int foo(int x, int y) { return x + y;}void invariant_hoist(int size) {    int x = 10;    int y = 5;    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {      foo(x, y); // hoistable    }  }
Bug_Explanation: The function call 'foo(x, y)' inside the 'invariant_hoist' method is loop-invariant and hoistable. This means that it has no side side effects (pure), has invariant arguments and result, and it is guaranteed to execute, i.e. it dominates all loop sources. However, this function call is inside a loop and could be hoisted out of the loop to improve performance. This is a potential optimization, but it may not always be correct to do so, especially in a multithreaded environment where the values of x and y could change.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered by modifying the values of x and y within the loop of the invariant_hoist method. This violates the invariant property of the function call, which assumes that the values of x and y remain constant throughout all iterations of the loop. However, in this test case, the values of x and y are modified within the loop, causing the bug to be triggered.
